c.tagline: A princely microstate capital tucked beneath alpine peaks.

taxi.fareNote: No metered public taxi fleet; fares are pre-agreed with local car/taxi services (e.g., calling ahead or via hotel).

emergency.note: Fire brigade is 118; general European emergency number 112 also works.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: Vaduz's tiny walkable core around Städtle promenade, with the Prince's castle above, government buildings, museums and the main shopping street; best for first-time visitors wanting everything on foot.

Liechtenstein's largest town and transport/business hub just north of Vaduz, with the national train station, more affordable lodging and dining, and easy bus links; suits budget travelers and those arriving by rail.
A quiet residential village south of Vaduz along the Rhine valley with vineyards and walking trails; suits travelers seeking a low-key, local-feeling base with easy bus access to the capital.

water.note: Among the highest-quality tap water in Europe; safe to drink directly from any tap or public fountain.

transit.pay: Buy single tickets or day passes from the driver (cash/card) or via the LIEmobil app; tickets also cover connecting Swiss PostBus/rail links to Sargans and Buchs. Liechtenstein has no railway passenger service of its own.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30am-midnight on most routes with reduced frequency on weekends; no night bus network.
transit.note: Liechtenstein has no airport or train station of its own; Schaan-Vaduz is the nearest rail-adjacent bus hub, and the country is entirely served by the LIEmobil bus network.

bus: PostBus connections to Switzerland and Austria

transit.m: Train to Sargans + bus 11/12/13 to Vaduz (~2h)

tip.r: Service is included in prices; rounding up or leaving small change is appreciated but not expected, as in Switzerland.

landmarks: Vaduz Castle
The private residence of Liechtenstein's royal family since 1938, this medieval hilltop castle overlooking the capital is the country's most photographed symbol.
Cathedral of St. Florin
This neo-Gothic red-brick cathedral with its slender spire serves as the principal Catholic church of Liechtenstein and a striking landmark in the city center.
Government Building (Regierungsgebäude)
This elegant early 20th-century building housing Liechtenstein's government sits prominently along Vaduz's main promenade, embodying the microstate's understated grandeur.
Vaduz City Hall (Rathaus)
A charming early-1900s civic building with distinctive architecture, this city hall anchors the historic core of Liechtenstein's tiny but stately capital.
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein
Housed in a striking black basalt-and-glass cube, this modern art museum holds an impressive collection of modern and contemporary works from the princely family.
Landtag (Parliament Building)
This sleek modern parliament building with a distinctive curved copper roof reflects Liechtenstein's blend of tradition and contemporary design along the city promenade.
Liechtenstein National Museum
Set in a former customs house and inn, this museum traces the principality's history, culture, and archaeology through engaging, compact exhibits.
Städtle
Vaduz's pedestrianized main street is lined with cafes, boutiques, and government buildings, making it the lively heart of the world's sixth-smallest country.
Peter-Kaiser-Platz
This central plaza named for a national statesman is a popular gathering spot framed by government architecture and mountain backdrops.
Red House (Rotes Haus)
This vine-covered, crimson-walled medieval manor house with a distinctive tower is one of Vaduz's oldest and most photogenic buildings.

train.note: Vaduz has no railway station. The nearest halt, Schaan-Vaduz (3 km away), sees only a limited weekday ÖBB S-Bahn shuttle between Buchs SG (Switzerland) and Feldkirch (Austria). For mainline and international trains, take a LIEmobil bus to Sargans or Buchs SG (Swiss SBB network) or Feldkirch (Austrian ÖBB network).

bus.note: FlixBus coaches stop at the Rheinpark Stadion car park on Vaduz's western edge, not in the town centre. Local LIEmobil buses (https://www.liemobil.li/en/) also cross the borders frequently to Sargans and Buchs in Switzerland and Feldkirch in Austria — handy for reaching mainline trains.

ferry.note: Liechtenstein is landlocked, so there are no ferries. The Rhine here is not navigable for passenger boats; the nearest lake boats are on Lake Constance, about an hour away.
